ups_type.description: UPS communication type: USB, SERIAL, or NET (networked UPS)

device_path.description: Device path (e.g., /dev/ttyS0) or host:port for network UPS

ups_name.description: Human-readable name for this UPS (used in logs and alerts)

timeout.description: Maximum time (seconds) UPS will power connected devices before forced shutdown

selftest_interval.description: Interval (minutes) between automatic UPS self-tests; 0 disables them

battery_level_percent.description: Minimum battery charge (%) that triggers forced shutdown if runtime estimate unavailable

min_runtime_minutes.description: Minimum remaining runtime (minutes) before forced shutdown

annoy_delay_minutes.description: Minutes to wait after power returns before resuming normal operations

announce_delay_minutes.description: Minutes to delay before sending first shutdown warning email

http_enabled.description: Enable built-in HTTP status server (allows viewing UPS status via web browser)

http_port.description: Port for HTTP status server (must be open in firewall)

http_host.description: IP address to bind HTTP server to (leave empty to bind to all interfaces)

mail_enabled.description: Enable email notifications on UPS events (e.g., power loss, low battery)

mail_address.description: Email address to receive UPS event notifications

logfile.description: Path to log file (empty or 'syslog' = use system syslog)

nis_enabled.description: Enable NIS (Network Information Service) daemon for remote status queries

nis_port.description: Port for NIS daemon (same as HTTP_PORT by default)

nis_ip.description: IP address to bind NIS daemon to (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces)

device_options.description: Additional device-specific options (e.g., baud rate for serial, like '-b 9600')

nis_allowed_hosts.description: List of hostnames or IP addresses allowed to query NIS status
